title: Prove commutative caller obstruction for the integer-shear target
body:
PR3905 proves an exact four-call minimum for the integer-shear target B=X²Y² in F2[G]. This contribution resolves one caller-transfer obligation: every unital algebra map from F2[G] into a commutative F2-algebra sends B to 1. The exact relation XY⁻¹X=Y⁻¹XY⁻¹ forces UV=1. For the selected additive carrier F2[M3(Q)], the order-four relation, domain property and augmentation additionally force both generator images to 1.

The theorem permits arbitrary algebra images, including polynomial encodings. It concerns entrywise scalar-algebra transfer; noncommutative matrix carriers and other encoding contracts remain outside scope. PR3905’s formal minimum remains valid. No native implementation, supplier bill, new kappa, or frontier change is claimed.

Evidence:
- Written universal proof; exact source-bound relation checks.
- Registered Python 3.12.14 replay passes, including the unchanged PR3905 verifier (85 shorter words, 47 distinct elements, four-call formal endpoint and restoration controls).
- Genuine F4 and dual-number quotient characters distinguish the hypotheses; an eight-point noncommutative action preserves B.
- Separate AI review independently reconstructs both characters by different methods and rejects seven mutations in normal and optimized Python. No human or formal-kernel review is claimed.
- An 11-file regular-only, read-only, inode-disjoint Git-free export passes both commands. Commit-byte and declared source-history preflights pass. The published tree equals the tested local tree.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/sl2z-commutative-caller-obstruction`.

The A5 perfectness method also extends to commutative algebra images; this adds the distinct integer-shear relation and additive-carrier corollary. Start with one complete four-call instance. The finite permutation control supplies no such bill. No continuing claim or larger word search is proposed.
